title: Sensex closes 2,009 points higher as oil slides after US midterms
dek: The Sensex ended 2.6% up at 79,310 and the Nifty 2.4% higher at 24,537 as Brent fell further, extending the indices' winning run to a sixth day.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Indian shares closed sharply higher on Thursday as oil prices extended their slide after the US midterm elections, with the Sensex gaining 2,008.61 points, or 2.60%, to end at 79,310.01.

The NSE Nifty 50 rose 576 points, or 2.40%, to 24,536.60, according to closing reports. It was the sixth straight gain for both indices. Car makers and lenders led: the Nifty Auto index rose 4.14%, Nifty Financial Services 3.99% and Nifty Realty 3.52%. ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank and Bajaj Finance added the most points to the Nifty, while Apollo Hospitals, ONGC, NTPC and Coal India fell. Smaller companies lagged, with the Nifty Midcap 100 up 1.87% and the Smallcap 100 up 0.56%. Rising shares outnumbered falling ones by more than two to one.

Oil was the main driver. Brent crude fell to about $93.50 a barrel early on Thursday, from a high of $104.96 on Wednesday, and January Brent futures were at $96.15 around the market close, one report said. Traders read the Democrats' win in both houses of the US Congress as lowering the risk of further US escalation against Iran and of new disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. India imports most of its crude oil, so cheaper oil eases pressure on inflation and the rupee. Gold futures on MCX rose 1.19% to Rs 1,44,933 per 10 grams.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday that two more tankers and a tugboat were burning in the strait, so the risk to supply has not gone away. The market's next big cue is the Hormuz situation and the remaining company results for the September quarter.
